observation_summary: The @InjectMocks annotation was failing to use available property setters for dependency injection, defaulting to direct field access instead.
reasoning_summary: The fix introduces a new conditional logic step to attempt injection via a BeanPropertySetter before falling back to the existing FieldSetter. This is a change in the procedural strategy for dependency injection, which fits the definition of an Algorithm/Method defect.
evidence_used: The fix adds a conditional check: if (!new BeanPropertySetter(fieldInstance, field).set(matchingMock)) { ... }
The original code only performed field injection: new FieldSetter(fieldInstance, field).set(matchingMock);
The bug report states: '@InjectMocks should carry out their work by the method (and not by field) if available'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds an 'if' statement, the primary purpose is to implement a new injection strategy (trying setters first), not just to validate existing data.
This is a local procedural change to the injection logic, not a design-level capability omission.
